## Design

### 2026-10-20 – In this session, I came up with and sketched up a design for my MindfieldMania MP3 player.

**3h**

In this session, I came up with and sketched up a design for my MindfieldMania MP3 player.

![IdeaSketch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/db9c420f4a7ee31aa32928d1a883d54efd533bb850fcad05f1d738c8b69932cb.jpg)

It is going to play Vsauce's mindfield intro on the click of a button. I will use this for the moments when someone says something really deep and needs recognition for their vsaucity.

It will use a DFPlayer to play the intro, paired with an arduino nano to control it.

![DFPlayer](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/f0a67687e3f847204d973dd1d1bf1d299fe929b24ce1796c7a82354ef3653cf8.png)

For my previous 2 projects, I was able to use a USB cable to power the boards. In this project - as the player will be portable - I will use a 18650 lithium battery paired with a TP4056 charge board and an MT3607 voltage booster to power the system. I ordered these parts, after doing some research and selecting them.

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 180754](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/97608a8df40097cd54fe0178fcce566df846959acf5ee93c7b8756e82dbe1d3a.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 180808](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/04b5db878facd5fb9b99df4f831ff5ea844c485694e65e1ffb5884c44a602693.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 185626](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/3f72a27dcb20fbcf35da16efd7a6a7c17943c1c7974b7f105973f419cd3bb973.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 185641](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/59320198abadebcc69cfe684b5e1fac5705fc4c6b5ede826844f357a9e67fd2f.png)

Next steps are making the schematic, ordering  the DFPlayer, speaker, and button, and finding some code to fit my needs.

### 2026-10-22 – In this session, I made a case for the electronics in CAD. The basis of the design is a hexagon with filleted edges. There is a hole at the top for the 76mm speaker to fit in.

**4h**

In this session, I made a case for the electronics in CAD. The basis of the design is a hexagon with filleted edges. There is a hole at the top for the 76mm speaker to fit in.
Oh yeah I finally found one that will be big, and work with the DFPlayer's on board amp.

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 173638](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/baced05690ba8e9ca4ba588cf5d12ef9deda70e0c0ccfb594922b986d1fdefb4.png)

 There's also a hole for the USB charging port to go in, and a couple holes for switches. (One to turn on and off and one to play sound.)

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 172420](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/5183d3b9f9643c556cb726cb934c109de24066127020e3c15adf005b266608ac.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 172717](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/eb26db4b9f46ed6756ee688123098ee600db2292be20ba435ade4164e20febf4.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 173005](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/325d4c4e606799e3138ea5c732fd45d41844b9691f54c184ba335af7d4231c24.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 173508](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/280ebd6234ced8d6abb6db44564df110ab6d48f8d7838ebf845f5a99ce03f712.png)

I might have to change the size of the box, depending on how big the speaker is. The info on Jaycar's website doesn't give much information so I may go in and check with them later in the week. I looked at some code options online and I will likely adapt someone elses code. Or... it might finally be time for me to learn some Arduino IDE. I think it all depends on how much time I have.

**6h**

I decided that I needed to learn IDE so that I could make the project run smoother. I wanted the intro to play on the flick of a switch which would require some modifications to the code. Steamakersblocks did not have the DFPlayer so I had to learn some IDE to progress.
I watched a couple of tutorials on how to use Arduino IDE. I firstly made a light turn on. (Impressive right?)

![1000146756](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/bf43bafcaac5b0056b4d9f58ced4d5e544098e42f91d46fe5fc7e568d5d622c1.jpg)

Then, I expanded on that knowledge by making a light go on and then have another one go on in replacement. I took a video but these are screenshots from it as I can't upload videos here.

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 214913](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/3a55673614a6da57b3ad3da57ba497fa35078b716cc869e210aa5a213d9a1513.png)

I then experimented with an OLED screen because they are very useful and I will probably use them in a lot of projects. This also used to be a video. The screen goes to the left in real life.

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 215120](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/5dc61557ac604c8c649ff165a8b1929b5496251eb408291b6163f8548e3d885f.png)

I tried one last thing which was to incorporate a DHT11 sensor but it didn't work. The part was very old so that might have been the issue.

![1000146787](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/a1420540c2d0a3da43bace3e019352fa0ebefb43836d7b5a36908d8dc676b451.jpg)

In this session, I learnt a lot about Arduino. I also found out where I can find resources and libraries to help me in the future. Hopefully, I will be able to use IDE for all of my future Arduino projects, instead of relying on clunky Steamakersblocks.

### 2026-10-24 – I went to Jaycar to go and buy the speaker I will be using for this project. I wanted to make sure that I had the correct size, and that it would fit well.

**3.5h**

I went to Jaycar to go and buy the speaker I will be using for this project. I wanted to make sure that I had the correct size, and that it would fit well.

![WIN_20261025_13_37_33_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/8b806b2bfa8774e0c31d3ae11f77d40cb9813502790c9047cae14ee5602b5a6c.jpg)

The photo on Jaycar's website wasn't very accurate, so I thought it had a metal top. Because it's top has a cone and is soft, it would be very easy to break if it didn't have a shell blocking things from falling in. I redesigned the top of the model to include a bunch of hexagon holes instead of a large circular one. I didn't do the traditional tesselating pattern because it wouldn't be symmetrical and match the circular shape of the speaker. I used the circular pattern tool in Fusion360 to plot hexes instead.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 133151](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/0abdc09aafe896ac9f3f3326fe079cdc5a1239d437559a2a0238e4a4c736fe72.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 133517](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/7529b1a2158bc3775acce7c00768d43ff9cfb8258efa586c7766845dee971781.png)

I also changed the size to make sure that it will be able to hold all of the parts. I am quite sure that it will work but I can always change the size when the parts arrive. Because of the size change, the holes I put in for the speaker mount, switches and charge port were in the wrong position relative to the case. I moved them around to make sure they were still aligned in the center.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 133502](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/66779a6889046c52a0aaeaed7d57bdecf0e7771b914ddba01226c506845d605c.png)

Because I couldn't just place the speaker in as there is a mesh on top of it, I split the body to make the base and the lid. I will connect them with some glue.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 133942](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/4fda3ff29422b5dcf4b93f3c4357c496e79fa219962363edfd79f90000fb0b15.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 133946](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/56a02e194dbe3041e1296b92caf6f5d34a789b93b53e492373decc3e86b5dcae.png)
